sections.bio:
I’m a Full-Stack .NET, Cloud & AI Engineer with 11+ years of experience designing enterprise-grade, cloud-native systems using .NET, Azure, microservices, and modern AI capabilities.

My work increasingly focuses on building AI-powered systems, including GenAI and agent-based architectures, where intelligence is embedded into real-world applications, not just demos.

I’ve conducted 2.5K+ interviews globally across all levels, giving me a practical understanding of what separates average engineers from strong system thinkers.

What I focus on:

- Designing scalable, high-performance systems
- Building AI-integrated applications (GenAI, AI agents, AI systems)
- Simplifying complex architecture decisions
- Developing cloud-first, reliable solutions

Across domains like Industrial Automation, Healthcare, and Enterprise IT, I’ve worked on modernizing systems with a strong emphasis on performance, reliability, and long-term maintainability.

Beyond building systems, I mentor developers to:

move from coding → system thinking
understand real-world architecture decisions
grow into senior and architect roles

Core areas:

- Cloud-native architecture
- Microservices & distributed systems
- AI systems, GenAI, agentic AI architectures
- Azure, Kubernetes, DevOps
- .NET Core, APIs, modern web (Angular)
- Performance & scalability engineering

I believe in clear thinking, strong fundamentals, and building systems that actually scale.

🔥IEnumerable vs IQueryable in .NET 👇

The difference is not just the interface.

It’s about where the query runs.

❌ IEnumerable
→ Data is already loaded
→ Filtering happens in memory

✅ IQueryable
→ Builds an expression tree
→ Provider can translate the query
→ Filtering can happen at the data source

This matters when working with EF Core and large datasets.

Save this one for your next .NET interview.

→ Layered

→ CQRS
→ Event-Driven

The goal isn't to pick the most complex architecture.

🔥Not all cryptography solves the same problem.

In .NET, know the difference:

→ Hashing → integrity / one-way transformation
→ AES → symmetric encryption
→ RSA → asymmetric encryption
→ Data Protection → application-level protection

Choosing the wrong primitive can turn a security feature into a security problem.

🔥Vector databases help applications search by meaning, not just keywords.

The basic flow:

→ Data
→ Embeddings
→ Vector Database
→ Similarity Search

This is the foundation behind many:
• Semantic search
• RAG applications
• Recommendation systems

Once you understand embeddings, vector databases become much easier to reason about.
